harness: Isolated HTTP handlers, tool-less director, three workers and two integration checks in OpenShell MicroVMs; synthetic public numbers fixture only.
fixture: Parallel iterative factorial and Fibonacci refactors followed by an unchanged-tree review; four protected unittest cases.

assignments:
Goal: Refactor factorial.py so the factorial function computes its result with an iterative loop instead of recursion.

Constraints:
- Only modify factorial.py. Do not touch fibonacci.py or any other file (including tests).
- Keep the public API exactly the same: same function name(s), signature(s), return values and module-level exports.
- Preserve the existing input validation unchanged: same accepted inputs, same exception types and messages for invalid input (e.g. negative numbers, non-integers, bools if currently rejected).
- Remove the recursive call; use a simple for/while loop accumulating the product. Edge cases such as 0 and 1 must still return 1 (or whatever the current behavior is).
- Match the existing code style, naming and comment density; keep docstrings accurate.
- Do not add new dependencies or configuration.

Verification: run `python3 -m unittest -v` and ensure all tests pass.

Goal: Refactor fibonacci.py so the fibonacci function computes its result in linear time with an iterative loop (no recursion, no exponential re-computation).

Constraints:
- Only modify fibonacci.py. Do not touch factorial.py or any other file (including tests).
- Keep the public API exactly the same: same function name(s), signature(s), return values, indexing convention (e.g. fib(0) and fib(1) values) and module-level exports.
- Preserve the existing input validation unchanged: same accepted inputs, same exception types and messages for invalid input (e.g. negative numbers, non-integers, bools if currently rejected).
- Implement with an O(n) loop keeping the two previous values (O(1) extra space); do not use recursion or memoization caches.
- Match the existing code style, naming and comment density; keep docstrings accurate.
- Do not add new dependencies or configuration.

Verification: run `python3 -m unittest -v` and ensure all tests pass.

Goal: Read-only review of the verified combined repository tree. Do NOT modify, create or delete any file.

Check:
- factorial.py: factorial is computed with an iterative loop (no recursion); input validation and public API (names, signatures, return values, exceptions and messages) are preserved; edge cases like 0 and 1 behave as before.
- fibonacci.py: fibonacci runs in linear time with an iterative loop (no recursion, no exponential work); input validation and public API (names, signatures, indexing convention, exceptions and messages) are preserved.
- No unrelated changes were introduced in either file.

Run `python3 -m unittest -v` and confirm all tests pass. Report findings in prose only; leave the tree exactly unchanged.
